body.statement: At \(P=P^{\diamond}\), the declared objects satisfy \(X_0=\{-1/2,1/2\}\), \(H=\{(-1/2,1/2),(1/2,-1/2)\}\), \(g=0\), \(A=1/2\), \(T=0\), and \(\nu_P=\tfrac12\delta_{-1/2}-\tfrac12\delta_{1/2}\). The obstacle endpoints are \(\ell_P(-1/2)=\ell_P(1/2)=-1/2\) and \(r_P(-1/2)=r_P(1/2)=1/2\), so \(\mathcal C_P=\{u:|u(-1/2)|\le1/2,\ |u(1/2)|\le1/2\}\) and \(\Theta(P)=[-1,1]\). For every such \(u\), the displayed schedules of \(Q_u^{\diamond}\) preserve \(P^{\diamond}\), satisfy \(|b_u^{\diamond}|\le1\), obey parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and, because their period difference is \(u(X)\) at every dose, also obey the stronger all-\(I\) equality, have \(m_{Q_u^{\diamond}}=u\), and attain \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=u(1/2)-u(-1/2)\). The endpoint assignment \(u(-1/2)=1/2,u(1/2)=-1/2\) gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=-1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=-1\); reversing the two signs gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=1\). This is a heterogeneous two-point baseline design with both signs of treatment change, not the common-zero-baseline scalar design.
body.justification: The calculation makes the non-singleton frontier and its full-law attainment visible in the smallest genuinely heterogeneous-baseline design.
body.gap: The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval in de Chaisemartin et al. (2024) has one baseline and one scalar nuisance; this example has two baselines, opposite change signs, a signed objective, and distinct affine completions.
body.consumer: The worked law is a unit test for endpoint software and a transparent template for explaining support-driven partial identification in applications.
